title: A determination of whether the dimensionless constants of physics are calculable

concept.text: Strings 2000 problem 1 (proposed by David Gross): are all the measurable dimensionless parameters that characterize the physical universe calculable in principle, or are some merely determined by historical or quantum mechanical accident and uncalculable? Sources given: https://preskill.caltech.edu/millennium.html ; https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v54.i10.14_2.online.pdf ; https://x.com/martinmbauer/status/1779906631003697211.

change_log.change: Added by hand to PHY on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: One of the ten Physics Problems for the Next Millennium chosen at the Strings 2000 conference (University of Michigan) by a panel of Michael Duff, David Gross and Edward Witten; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: Calculability of the dimensionless constants of physics
page.definition: A determination of whether physical laws fix every measurable dimensionless constant—a number independent of measurement units, such as a mass ratio—or leave at least one dependent on historical conditions or a quantum outcome. Calculating a probability distribution must be distinguished from calculating the particular value observed.

goal.need: A 2006 inventory counted 26 independent inputs for particle physics and five more for cosmology. Better measurements narrow their uncertainties but leave their values unexplained. Deriving a value would turn it into an independent test: for example, two measured interaction strengths could predict a third if the forces have a common origin. If a value varies across regions, a theory could instead explain how likely we are to observe it, provided it accounts for both how often the value occurs and where observers can form.

figures.caption: Inputs in Tegmark and colleagues' 2006 inventory
figures.note: This is the paper's model-dependent inventory, not a fixed count for every possible theory. Dimensional quantities are expressed in Planck units.

statements.body: National Research Council, Committee on Elementary-Particle Physics
statements.quote: What determines this structure and the values of these parameters?
statements.context: The question concerns the Standard Model's particle masses, interactions and independent parameters, discussed in Chapter 3.

statements.quote: Are all the (measurable) dimensionless parameters that characterize the physical universe calculable in principle or are some merely determined by historical or quantum mechanical accident and uncalculable?
statements.context: David Gross submitted the question. Michael Duff, Gross and Edward Witten selected it as problem 1 in “Physics Problems for the Next Millennium.”

completion.title: An empirically supported theory establishes whether all dimensionless constants are fixed by physical laws.
completion.criterion: A peer-reviewed theoretical result, independently checked and supported by discriminating observations, establishes either that physical laws fix every measurable dimensionless parameter or that at least one retains historical or quantum contingency within the supported theory. The argument identifies any remaining initial conditions and vacuum choices. A numerical fit, an uncompleted calculation or the existence of several mathematical solutions does not establish contingency.
completion.set_by: Atlas; operational interpretation of Strings 2000 problem 1. The conference published the question without an adjudication procedure.
completion.basis: Searches of the Strings 2000 problem list, National Research Council discussions, fundamental-constants reviews and string-phenomenology reviews found the question and partial research criteria, but no published adjudication procedure. This test retains Gross's two possible answers. Its conclusion is conditional on the empirically supported theory; finite measurements cannot establish a statement about every conceivable theory.

milestones.title: A string vacuum reproduces the Standard Model gauge group and chiral matter spectrum.
milestones.criterion: A four-dimensional string construction contains the Standard Model gauge group. For each representation under that group, the net chiral fermion count matches the Standard Model, including its three generations. Additional vector-like pairs are allowed because their left- and right-handed members cancel in the net count.
milestones.set_by: String-phenomenology model-building convention, described by Marchesano, Shiu and Weigand in Section 2.2. This benchmark concerns the string-theory route only.
milestones.threshold_quote: contain the SM gauge group and chiral spectrum and are absent of chiral exotics

milestones.title: One string vacuum combines the Standard Model, stabilised moduli and observed cosmology.
milestones.criterion: One four-dimensional string vacuum reproduces the Standard Model gauge group and particle content, including vector-like matter, and its pattern of fermion masses and mixing. In that same vacuum, all moduli, the fields describing continuous choices such as the size and shape of the extra dimensions, are stabilised, and the cosmology is consistent with observation.
milestones.set_by: String-phenomenology research criterion stated by Marchesano, Shiu and Weigand in Section 6. This benchmark concerns string compactifications only; the source supplies no numerical cosmological tolerance.
milestones.threshold_quote: combine all these features at the same time, with all moduli stabilized and incorporating a realistic cosmology.

milestones.title: An ensemble theory computes the joint probability distribution of its dimensionless constants.
milestones.criterion: For a theory in which constants can differ across regions, calculate the joint probability distribution of its dimensionless parameter vector. Specify where observations are sampled, such as at galaxies or observers. Weight the theory’s prior distribution of parameter values by the expected abundance of those reference objects at each set of values, then normalise the distribution.
milestones.set_by: Statistical-prediction criterion applied to ensemble cosmologies by Tegmark, Aguirre, Rees and Wilczek, Sections I.C and V. This is a criterion for ensemble theories, without a numerical acceptance cutoff.
milestones.threshold_quote: they are neither testable nor falsifiable unless their probabilistic predictions can be computed.

milestones.title: Independent measurements corroborate a theory's discriminating predictions for dimensionless constants.
milestones.criterion: Measurements not used to fit a candidate theory's predictions agree with its predicted constants or their joint distribution, including relevant selection effects. The observations distinguish that prediction from alternatives. No universal precision, significance or experimental sample-size threshold is specified.
milestones.set_by: Atlas; searches of the Strings 2000 problem statement, academy discussions and the cited prediction frameworks found no constants-specific experimental acceptance threshold. This operationalises their requirement to confront physical predictions with observation.

milestones.title: A grand unified model predicts the strong coupling from the two electroweak couplings.
milestones.criterion: Use the two electroweak gauge couplings measured at the Z-boson mass and the model’s common high-energy coupling condition to calculate the strong coupling at the Z-boson mass. Specify the particle spectrum, the prescription for defining the couplings and the corrections at particle mass thresholds. Reserve the measured strong coupling for comparison.
milestones.set_by: Gauge-unification convention described by Damien M. Pierce, sections 1–3, and tested with LEP data by Amaldi, de Boer and Fürstenau.
milestones.threshold_quote: one need only input two of the gauge couplings, then the third one can be predicted

not_found: No published adjudication procedure was found for deciding Strings 2000 problem 1.
No framework-independent laboratory-to-completion milestone sequence was found; the published theoretical benchmarks concern particular research routes.
No universal experimental precision or significance threshold was found for corroborating an explanation of dimensionless constants.
No academy or conference-panel statement was found disputing the value or feasibility of resolving the calculability question.

results.finding: F-theory construction: approximately 10^15 compactifications with the exact Standard Model chiral spectrum.
results.detail: The models have the Standard Model gauge group and three chiral generations. The count is an estimate; additional vectorlike matter may be present. These are theoretical constructions.
results.quote:
We present Oð1015Þ string compactifications with the exact chiral spectrum of the standard model of
particle physics.

results.finding: One compact type IIB quiver construction yields 3 net chiral Standard Model generations.
results.quote:
The resulting 3 family chiral spectrum agrees with our ﬁeld theory expectation on the left
of ﬁgure 7.

results.finding: One type IIB compactification geometry yields de Sitter minima at internal volumes of order 10²–10³.
results.detail: Explicit fixing of the axio-dilaton and complex-structure moduli was left open, and open-string moduli were only partly fixed. The cosmology discussion identifies compatible scales and possible mechanisms.
results.quote:
Let us also mention that we managed to obtain dS minima at values of the volume
of order V ∼102–103 which are not extremely large, but still large enough to keep a nu-
merical, even if not parametric, control over quantum corrections.

results.finding: The axion ensemble models halo selection across 4 cosmological parameters. No empirical sample enters this calculation.
results.detail: The plotted marginal integrates over dark energy and approximates solar-system stability with an upper cutoff on halo density.
results.quote:
the theory predicts a 2-dimensional distribution in the
(ρΛ, ξ)-plane of which Figure 9 is the marginal distribu-
tion

results.finding: For one observed universe, the matter abundance of ≈4 eV per photon agrees with the selection-weighted axion model.
results.detail: The upper halo-density cutoff controls the high-abundance tail. The paper also reports qualitative agreement with the observed abundance for a WIMP estimate.
results.quote:
The dotted vertical line shows our observed value ξ ≈ 4 eV, in
good agreement with the prediction.

results.finding: About 10¹⁵ F-theory compactifications realize the Standard Model gauge group with 3 net chiral generations.
results.detail: The ensemble size is estimated from toric triangulations. The construction gives the chiral index for each matter representation.
results.quote:
In summary, we have constructed a class of elliptically
fibered Calabi-Yau fourfolds that gives rise in F theory to
the standard model gauge group and matter representations
with three chiral generations.

results.finding: About 10¹⁵ F-theory compactifications realize 3 chiral generations and allow the Standard Model Yukawa couplings.
results.detail: The Yukawa couplings depend on moduli. The paper leaves the multiplicities of Higgs doublets and other charged vector-like pairs open.
results.quote:
All these models come equipped with
moduli-dependent quark and lepton Y ukawa couplings, as
well as gauge coupling unification at the compactifica-
tion scale.

results.finding: About 10¹⁵ F-theory compactifications exhibit gauge coupling unification with hypercharge normalization 5/3.
results.detail: The equality is independent of Kähler moduli. The compactification scale and the individual coupling values depend on moduli stabilization.
results.quote:
Moreover, all models exhibit gauge coupling unification at
the compactification scale, compatible with the existence of
a complex structure deformation to a geometry realizing the
Pati-Salam model with unified gauge coupling [11,15].

results.finding: One 5D supersymmetric SU(5) model predicts a strong coupling at MZ of 0.118 ± 0.003.
results.detail: The abstract gives the central value. Equation (24) gives the range across the model’s superpartner mass scale. The ±0.003 uncertainty comes from unknown physics at and above the cutoff.

results.finding: Minimal supersymmetric SU(5) predicts αs(MZ) > 0.123 across the specified parameter region. Sample size is inapplicable to this calculation.
results.detail: The minimal SU(5) bound uses the smallest color-triplet Higgs mass allowed by nucleon-decay constraints to minimize the predicted strong coupling.
results.quote: αs(MZ) > 0.123 (Minimal SU(5) , m ˜q ≤ 1 TeV, m t = 170 GeV),

results.finding: Both of the two explicit heterotic compactifications yield the Standard Model gauge group and three net chiral generations.
results.detail: The authors compute the spectrum from line-bundle cohomology and apply the discrete Wilson-line projection. Their assumptions for fitting fermion masses and mixing are separate from the reported chiral spectrum.
results.quote: In both cases, the massless spectra consist of three chiral families of quarks and leptons, along with a single vector-like pair of Higgs doublets and several singlet fields.

results.finding: Toy inflationary ensemble with two varying dimensionless parameters and no finite sample gives P(y < y*) = 0.0005.
results.detail: The model uses a flat prior for positive Λ, holds other parameters fixed, and uses collapsed galactic mass as a proxy for observer abundance. The quoted probability is a marginal of the joint distribution.

results.finding: OPAL measured a change in Δα of 440 × 10⁻⁵ using 10,227,352 small-angle Bhabha events.
results.detail: The final fit used the right calorimeter and corrected the angular spectrum for bin-by-bin acceptance. The analysis measures the change across the accepted momentum range.

results.finding: ATLAS multijet correlations gave a fitted strong coupling αₛ(m_Z) = 0.1175 in 139 fb⁻¹ of proton–proton collisions.
results.quote:
A simultaneous fit to all transverse energy-energy correlation distributions across different kinematic regions yields a value of
\( {\alpha}_{\textrm{s}}\left({m}_Z\right)=0.1175\pm 0.0006{\left(\exp .\right)}_{-0.0017}^{+0.0034}\left(\textrm{theo}.\right) \)

goal.need = "A 2006 inventory counted 26 independent inputs for particle physics and five more for cosmology. Better measurements narrow their uncertainties but leave their values unexplained. Deriving a value would turn it into an independent test: for example, two measured interaction strengths could predict a third if the forces have a common origin. If a value varies across regions, a theory could instead explain how likely we are to observe it, provided it accounts for both how often the value occurs and where observers can form.". Reason: The current rationale gives the parameter count but omits what an independent prediction would let physicists test and what an observer-dependent probability would mean.
